chose: python parity domain-match mirrors the TS leftmost-root rule: registry.TOOL_NAMES does NOT count as enumerating TOOL_NAMES; sorted()/list()/set() wrappers unwrap first
over: substring/word-boundary matching of the domain name anywhere in the loop expression
because: the TS branch checks iterTargetOf(...).root === domain, and the root of a property chain is its LEFTMOST identifier — matching looser on the python side would let a .py oracle pass where the identical TS oracle fails, breaking the verdict-parity the mission requires

chose: extracted pyAnchorBlock/pyDomains out of analyzePythonOracle and shared them with the new parity arm
over: duplicating the def/class anchor + indent-block regexes inside analyzePythonParity
because: a second spelling of the anchor discipline is exactly the duplicated-domain defect this repo's own redundancy module exists to flag; the refactor is behavior-identical and test/python-oracle.test.ts (7 tests) still passes

chose: python redundancy sites: module-level dict literals, Enum class bodies, all-string list/tuple/set constants, match-case labels, and per-def if/elif == chains — nothing else
over: comprehensions, dict()/frozenset()/set() constructor calls, function-local dicts, string-prefixed literals (r/b/f), and 'x in (a,b,c)' membership tuples
because: python has no compiler behind it, so the typeLink suppression that absorbs TS false positives can never fire on a .py pair — precision must be earned upstream; any form the line-scan cannot read unambiguously yields NO site rather than a wrong one, per the module header's wall-of-candidates rationale

over: respelling the test_*.py/_test.py convention inside collectSites; leaving python test files scannable as domain surface
because: novelty.ts's isTestPath only knows TS test paths and a sibling agent owns that file; a hand-copied domain inside a .py oracle is oracle-domain.ts's finding, not redundancy's — same rule the TS side already enforces, and the NOISE_DIRS import precedent says share the spelling
